findings.detail: Training items are split into deciles by rank of occurrence count, and r/p values are likewise assigned bins by rank. This is not a fitted set of frequency-decile/quantile value boundaries: tied values can be split across bins according to item order. For example, several items with identical (f,u,r,p) can receive different suffixes when a frequency/shape group crosses a rank cut. This adds arbitrary item-ID/order information instead of a signature determined by the specified demand statistics.
findings.reproduction: Supply a frame with at least 10 active items whose counts tie, or a frequency-decile group with identical r and p values spanning a rank cut; inspect returned suffixes for items with identical statistics. Stable sorting preserves input item index, so identical statistics can receive different bins.
findings.correction: Fit numeric decile and within-decile quantile cut points on training items only, then apply those frozen boundaries to values; define deterministic tie handling that does not split equal-valued items.
